sections.overview: This Central American cichlid is endemic to the Pacific slope of southern Honduras. Its scientific name commemorates brothers George and Peter Hogaboom, who helped collect the type series.
sections.identification: Greyish flanks bear seven black bars, a fainter head bar and a rounded spot at the tail base; juveniles may have a spot within the fourth bar. FishBase reports 15 cm standard length for a male or unsexed fish. No dependable height, width, mass or sex-specific length was found.
sections.habitat: It occurs in the Choluteca and Negro river drainages on Honduras’s Pacific slope. FishBase records freshwater and brackish-water occurrence in a tropical climate.
sections.diet: The original account reports no prey or stomach analyses, so the wild diet remains poorly documented.
sections.behavior: Field observers watched three pairs guard young over nests and actively protect fry in clear, flowing water.
sections.reproduction: Roe was well developed in January–May. In April, pairs guarded young above cleared nests among rounded stones, in a clear current 1.8–3 m deep.
sections.ecology: The 2009 Honduran checklist extended its documented range beyond the lower Choluteca to the Río Negro, but still found it only in this Pacific-slope region. The original paper described it as moderately abundant in several settings where water was sufficiently deep.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment lists Amphilophus hogaboomorum as Data Deficient (DD), assessed in 2020. Its restricted Honduran range is clear, but the available assessment status does not support assigning a more precise level of extinction risk here.

sources.title: The fishes of the Choluteca drainage of southern Honduras — Carr & Giovannoli, 1950
